before.title: 4.0L Inline-6 Exhaust Manifold Cracking
before.description: The cast iron exhaust manifold on the 4.0L AMC/Jeep inline-6 engine is prone to cracking from thermal stress cycling. The manifold design does not accommodate thermal expansion well, and cracks develop between the exhaust ports, typically between cylinders 3-4 or 5-6. Cracked manifolds cause exhaust leaks that are loudest on cold startup and may quiet down as the manifold expands when hot. The exhaust leak can cause a ticking or hissing sound that is often mistaken for a lifter or valve issue. Broken exhaust manifold bolts are extremely common and can complicate the repair.
symptoms: Ticking or hissing exhaust leak noise, loudest on cold startup
Exhaust smell in engine bay or cabin
Reduced engine performance
Check engine light with catalyst efficiency codes
Noise diminishes as engine warms up

citations.description: Comanche 4.0L exhaust manifold cracking discussion and repair guide
4.0L exhaust manifold replacement and bolt extraction tips

communityRecommendations.text: Soak the exhaust manifold bolts with PB Blaster for several days before attempting removal - these bolts WILL break if not properly prepared. Heat cycling with a torch also helps
An aftermarket header (Banks Power or Flowtech) is a better long-term solution than another OEM manifold - the stock casting design is inherently flawed for thermal cycling

communityRecommendations.content: Exhaust manifold gasket set seals exhaust leaks at the head
Exhaust manifold stud kit replaces broken or corroded studs

before.title: Floor Pan and Frame Rust-Through
before.description: The Jeep Comanche (MJ platform) is extremely susceptible to floor pan and frame rust, especially in salt-belt states. The driver and passenger foot wells, rear cab corners, and bed floor are the primary rust-through areas. The unibody construction means that floor pan rust is structural and affects vehicle safety. Water intrusion through deteriorated door and window seals accelerates the corrosion. Many surviving Comanches have been lost to rust rather than mechanical failure. Rust repair requires cutting out affected sections and welding in new metal patches.
before.solution: Inspect the entire cab floor, rocker panels, cab corners, rear frame sections, leaf-spring/shackle mounts, and bed supports by removing carpet and undercoating, then probe all suspect areas with a pick or hammer to identify thin metal and hidden perforation. Any rust-through or heavily scaled structural metal should be cut back to solid steel and repaired with welded replacement floor pans, patch panels, or fabricated 16-18 gauge steel sections; treat surrounding areas with rust converter or epoxy primer, seam sealer, cavity wax, and replace leaking door/window seals to stop future water intrusion. If the frame rails, spring mounts, or major unibody sections are severely compromised, professional structural repair or donor-section replacement is required, and some trucks may be uneconomical to save. Typical costs range from about $500-$1,500 for localized patch repairs to $3,000-$8,000+ for extensive floor, cab corner, and structural rust restoration.
symptoms: Visible rust holes in floor pans
Water intrusion into cabin during rain
Soft or spongy floor when pressed
Rust bubbling under paint on cab corners and rocker panels
Structural weakness visible during inspection

citations.title: Extremely Rusted Floor Suggestions - Comanche Club
Replacing Floor Pans in the Comanche - BleepinJeep

communityRecommendations.text: Inspect underneath thoroughly before buying any Comanche - floor pan rust is structural on the unibody MJ and can make the vehicle unsafe. Poke suspicious areas with a screwdriver to test integrity
POR-15 and Eastwood Rust Encapsulator are the best products for treating existing rust before it becomes a hole - annual underbody inspection and treatment is essential for salt-belt Comanches

communityRecommendations.content: POR-15 rust preventive coating stops rust permanently
Rust-Oleum rust converter spray for treating corroded panels
Dorman weatherstrip seal prevents water leaks and wind noise
3M Super Weatherstrip Adhesive for reattaching loose seals

before.title: Renix Fuel Injection System Sensor Failures
before.description: The 1990 Comanche with the 4.0L uses the Renix (Renault/Bendix) fuel injection system, which is less reliable than the later Chrysler MPFI system used from 1991+. The Renix system relies on several sensors that fail with age: the coolant temperature sensor (CTS), throttle position sensor (TPS), and manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor. Failed sensors cause hard starting, rough idle, poor fuel economy, and stalling. The wiring harness connectors also corrode, causing intermittent issues that mimic sensor failure.
before.solution: Replace the CTS, TPS, and MAP sensors as a set — they are inexpensive and the labor overlaps. Clean all wiring harness connectors with electrical contact cleaner and apply dielectric grease. For 1990 models, consider upgrading to the 1991+ Chrysler MPFI system (often called a "Renix to HO swap") which uses a more reliable ECU and simplified sensor array. Replace the O2 sensor at the same time.
symptoms: Hard starting especially when cold
Rough or hunting idle
Stalling when coming to a stop
Poor fuel economy (under 15 mpg)
Hesitation or stumble during acceleration
Check engine light intermittently

citations.title: YouTube - How to Diagnose and Replace Renix Fuel Injection Sensors on Jeep Comanche 4.0L

communityRecommendations.text: The #1 fix for any drivability issue on a Renix 4.0 is replacing the CTS with a new Mopar sensor. The Renix CTS uses a completely different resistance curve from the HO CTS — do NOT interchange them.

communityRecommendations.content: Bosch fuel injector set — OEM replacement for precise fuel delivery
Chevron Techron fuel injector cleaner — restores injector flow
